reviews.text: Played the game a little bit so far. The graphics style is very satisfying and I love the idea going on for game play with choosing cards and loading the gun. However it feels more like a grind of repetitious action sequences rather than a full experience game. I think it would be much more enjoyable if there were more story elements like cut scenes and the occasional extra puzzle or dialogue based choice for the user. It would add a lot more fun and variation to the progression of the game. Its always fun to gain a new ability or card, but I feel it's kind of rushed in this game. Seemed to be pushing a new type of bullet every battle early on and extending the battle encounters and time spent on a zone rather than progressing the story. Now I have not finished the game yet, so I can't say for sure if it picks up the pace later on. I shall continue to play it and if my opinion changes, then so shall my review.

It's free, and for that, why not check it out? That said, it definitely has some serious balancing, progression, and pacing issues that are ignored in other "reviews". If I paid a couple dollars I wouldn't be frustrated for obvious reasons, but this game is definitely not worth the indie standard, which is why it is free. Healing and sustain functions are so sparse and/or ineffectual that they are rendered pointless. Damage is the only thing that matters because it is tied to the inappropriately labeled "parry" ability (which is really just a block function), a decision that while being novel, makes little sense. There is also the issue of methods the player character employs that NPCs do not employ, and vice-versa. The idea that not having a bullet in the chamber at the end of a turn delivers damage to the player also makes little sense. Sure, it's interesting, but that is a band-aid for an otherwise dull experience. All of these things contribute to the greatest issue, which is that the "meta deck" for the cards the player has unlocked is glaring easy to identify as you progress through the game. The odds that you survive is more so based on luck, rather than strategy or experience with card play-order variations from the five round chamber, with the chamber being the most unique set piece of the game. It has potential, no thanks to balancing, with hats off to the creativity.

This game's gameplay is fun at first, but gets boring after a while due to repetitive card types, overuse of text instead of visuals to explain basic things, and lack of animations. Additionally, it has stupid gimmick cards that can only be used to give 2 damage when it is in slot 4 and the opponent is getting sloppy from your mother. You end up having to not use 70% of the cards you get because they are all useless and too situational, and not in an enjoyable way. You also are cursed by the game to take an insane amount of damage for things that you CANT DEFEND AGAINST (for example, both enemies attack after giving you the scorching bullet.) It is anti-player and anti-fun. There's also nowhere to heal, once you raise your max health in the one section you can't heal for the next 50 miles, and healing is important because of the BS damage. Also, the scorching bullet deserves its own section. This is the worst mechanic that I have seen in a videogame all year and I do not exaggerate that. It stops you from actually defending or attacking as I mentioned earlier. It IS anti-player. It is not interesting to deal with, it just takes almost all of your stamina. If this game cost even half a dollar people would stop ignoring its flaws. This game feels like it was made while one developer was trying to make a decent game and the other was using mass amounts of illegal substances.

I like the game for its strategy focus, but by god does luck LITERALLY shoot you in the head at times. Despite my many runs I've never managed to get past a zone with two baddies and considering how close it always gets regardless, how the hell are you going to survive unless RNJesus blesses you with more than one health station, but even then the heals are pathetic and the health increase is only by 5+ which often makes a single turn round difference and in later stages of a fight, one turn can sometimes mean nothing.

The game looks nice, the drawings and atmosphere rend well, but it looks like an undevelopped early access game for now. There's something for sure, the mechanics and synergies with bullets are interesting and original, but there is nothing challenging for now. I just spent 5h rolling over everything, I didn't know what to spend my money on, I had all the bullets available (some in several ex) and nothing to go further. I finally had some "challenge" because i wanted to try a more "advanced" build (aka without all the obvious master bullets), otherwise it's a walk in a park. Enemies don't do much, if you pace yourself it's a no-brainer that becomes quiet boring rather quickly. Everything needs balancing, from the enemies (only 2 types who do always the same stuff, not enough rotations) and scaling of difficulty to what you can do with your build. Overall i was entertained, but i wouldn't come back nor recommend the game as such, it needs some work for sure.

".Forty-Five" is one of those games where the developer throws a whole bunch of genres in a blender and prays for success. Well, this wasn't a complete failure and there's still people playing it, so that's something. But while free, this is far from an excellent PC gaming experience. What do you do in the game? It's a CCG with a wild west theme, each card is a "bullet" that you load in your gun and then plod through a samey, repetitive Slay the Spire type procgen gamut and see if RNG is your friend or not... it gets repetitive immediately. And wow... the graphics... this whole thing could have been a webpage or Adobe Flash or something. No thanks. The game features really lacklustre 2D visuals (does the developer not know 3D graphics became mainstream in the mid-1990s?). Gamers don't spend thousands of dollars on gaming rigs and the latest 3D graphics cards to play 2D games. Even mobile phones and game consoles can do 3D graphics now. There's no excuse. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. On the matter of pricing and value for gamers, most "free" games on Steam aren't really free. There's often nasty mobile app cash shops, or content locked behind DLC, or donations being requested, or any other number of shady pricing schemes that could mislead gamers, but in this case I'm glad to say this really does appear to be a fully free game. Nothing demonstrates a developers belief in themselves and their work than giving it away without any remuneration. This is a service to themselves, and the gaming industry, and should be applauded. Of course, just because something is free, doesn't necessarily mean it's valuable, or something you might want to spend your time on. Bearing in mind that free games don't add +1 to your game collector count, should you bother adding this to your library and downloading it? This is a "maybe" experience... if you have a lot of free time on your hands and nothing else to do, why not? But for the purposes of a review, this isn't something I can say everyone must try. It's not quite there. Valve doesn't give us a "maybe" option in reviews, but if they did, that's what I'd choose for this.

It's free, and worth the price...? Maybe this deserves a positive on that level, I didn't *strongly* dislike the game, but if say I paid $3 for it I'd be a little disappointed, let's put it that way. That's not to say there's not some good stuff buried here; actually there's a lot to like. The concept is pretty great, and the theming. A pretty nifty system that has some nice quirks and nuances not at first apparent, the bullet system works pretty well. There's the bones of a fun game. Those easy to please might be fine with the bones. However, the enemy design is... well, it's rubbish. At least especially in the first act, you get enemies yo-yoing between pushovers that pose almost literally zero threat (that you can run up the score against to get shop-money, especially since half of them only build up trivial amounts of shield), to RNG-based enemies that fill up your 'energy' counter with junk, to damage that is rarely forecasted in amount (is it gonna be a 9, easy to "parry", or 20? Who knows?). There's no personality and the strategy is super hit and miss. The map supports backtracking, but doesn't pan properly so you often can't tell what's next. The attempt at a story atmosphere/vibe is bad, the graphics are bad (there's not even an option to scale the resolution... at all, so get used to fuzziness), the UI is unhelpful and fugly, I'm sure with a little work it could come off as charming but instead it comes off as an especially ambitious and intelligent middle school Flash project. In short, a bit more effort by the developer, and it's an extremely fun, positive-rated 5 dollar masterpiece, but in its present state it's more like a perpetual alpha, you get what you (don't) pay for, so set expectations accordingly. It vaguely reminds me of Astrea in the sense that order of play matters, but the depth doesn't feel there.
